# CLAIMs with `tags` `behavioral-integration`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Behavioral integration** — how an organism's many control systems come to act as one — action selection and competition between systems (habitual and goal-directed, automatic and willed), hierarchical and feedback control, intertemporal conflict and self-control, and evidence accumulation to a decision. One of four unities kept apart (ADR-024).

| [CLAIM-169](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-169.md) v2 | On Ainslie's account the population of interests is produced by desynchronized valuation, not given by a fixed architecture: an agent is many interests over a choice only as far as its valuations of that choice cross within the choice's horizon | The record's reading of [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md), made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. | [CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md) | Preference reversal is not yet disunity: interests that govern a choice at disjoint times glue, and a self is divided over a choice only on an overlap, which the agent's prediction of its own later valuation creates | Take an agent's interests as sections over contexts of choice, each governing the windows of time in which its valuation ranks first. If the windows do not overlap, the sections glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)): someone who prefers the diet in the morning and the cake at night is a time-indexed preference, not a divided self. Division needs an overlap, a choice on which both interests bear at once. On Ainslie's account that overlap is made by recursive self-prediction: the present choice is valued as a forecast of the later ones, so the later interest's valuation enters the present context. That is where intertemporal bargaining happens, and it is the coupling [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) found missing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-261](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-261.md) | Synchronization of an agent's interests is desirable, but not necessary for acting as one: internal conflict shows a human agent acting while its interests stay divided | The owner's answer to [QUESTION-078](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-078.md). Synchronization is still better when it is available: nothing has to be overridden, and [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) says that is why flow is effortless. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-262](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-262.md) | Whether an agent's regimes are coordinated by discrete switches or by continuous reorganization depends on how the agent is constituted; both occur | The owner's answer to [QUESTION-079](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-079.md): both forms are possible, and which one an agent shows depends on its constitution. An agent made of a population whose choices accumulate like a drift-diffusion process reorganizes continuously. Twitch Plays Pokémon approximates one, best in democracy mode with the tally visible as votes arrive. The consequence for [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md)'s transition test is that it must be stated per constitution. A missing switch counts against coordination only in an agent built to switch. | Proposed |
